newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-SAMMER SUFFERS FURTHER INJURY BLOW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAMMER SUFFERS FURTHER INJURY BLOW.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund's hopes of intensifying their German championship campaign in the important final month before the winter break have been hit by another injury to Matthias Sammer.
Sammer, Germany's most influential player at this year's European championship, has not been able to play for the reigning champions for eight weeks because of a complicated leg muscle tear.
The former East German was expected to return for his 100th Bundesliga game in Dortmund's home match with Karlsruhe on Saturday but is now almost certain to miss the clash because of a bruised thigh.

"It is tough for me," Sammer said. "But I see no reason to start cursing everything just because I have missed so many games. A lot of players have to retire early and I have made it to 28 without any problems."
The Bundesliga is due to take its two-month winter break on December 7. Often in the past the team which is on top of the Bundesliga at halfway has gone on to win the title.
Dortmund midfielder Andy Moeller, also a key part of Germany's successful Euro 96 campaign, agrees that it is a pyschological boost to win what the Germans call the "Autumn title".
"We want to be on top again so we can go into the break as the number one," Moeller said.

Franz Beckenbauer, Germany's former World Cup-winning captain and coach who is now chairman of rivals Bayern Munich, regards Sammer as the best libero since he made the position his own in the 1960s and 1970s.

Dortmund, who are presently fourth, have certainly missed Sammer's influence in the first half of the season. At least the winter break will give him the chance to regain 100 percent fitness for the rest of the season.
On Saturday, the reigning champions, who are unbeaten at home, should be able to welcome back former German international striker Karlheinz Riedle after 11 weeks out with a serious back problem.

Leaders Bayern, one point ahead of second-placed VfB Stuttgart, travel on Saturday to Freiburg who are struggling at the bottom of the table and were knocked out of the German Cup quarter-finals by VfB after a penalty shoot-out on Wednesday.
Stuttgart play hosts on Saturday to promoted Bochum, one of the biggest surprises of the season who also need to bounce back after an unlucky 2-1 cup defeat by Hamburg in midweek.
